briefings.headline: Be selective, then attack deGrom’s fastball
briefings.message: Jacob deGrom is the high-confidence expected starter. Left-handed hitters, look for fastballs; right-handed hitters, stay ready for his breaking balls. Make him earn outs—don’t expand on the slider or changeup, which produce whiff rates of 41.2% and 43.7%. If he exits, be ready for the Rangers’ available rested left- and right-handed bullpen options.
reminders: Hunt fastballs; take offspeed unless it is a strike.
Stay disciplined against the slider and changeup.
Josh Lowe is rest-suggested but available for a late running opportunity.

briefings.headline: Change speeds and keep their best bats off predictable fastballs
briefings.message: Walbert Ureña starts, with a 90-pitch limit and a target of 5.0 innings. Use the changeup below the zone to Carter and avoid giving Nimmo or Pederson a hittable fastball; their matchup expected xwOBA figures are 0.348 and 0.318. Mix breaking balls and change speeds to Jung. In a close late lead, Suter can handle a key left-handed pocket, Bachman can bridge, and Yates closes; use Farris for length if Ureña exits early.
reminders: Use the changeup as the main chase pitch to lefties.
Avoid predictable fastballs to Nimmo and Pederson.
Save Yates for a late lead or the highest-leverage finish.

briefings.headline: Stay flexible behind Ureña and protect the late-game leverage plan
briefings.message: The lineup is built for the high-confidence expected starter, Jacob deGrom: prioritize left-handed fastball hunters Schanuel, Meckler, and Walton. Ureña starts over Soriano; his overall season xwoba_allowed is 0.281, and the plan targets 5.0 innings with a 90-pitch limit. Keep the bullpen flexible: Suter for a key left-handed pocket, Bachman to bridge, and Yates for a late lead. Lowe is rest-suggested but available; consider him for a late running chance. Peraza can replace Guzman defensively after Guzman’s final at-bat.
